Design

Repeatable content production

Routine zones, enemies, items, quests and recipes should be authored through validated data and Blueprint-exposed references.

On this page
Factory sequenceDensity measurementsDefinition validationExpansion checklist

Factory sequence

  1. Write a short content brief with player goal, connected zones, level range, travel targets and art/license needs.
  2. Create stable IDs and catalog rows using existing schemas; register dependencies and missing-art status. Do not add C++ because one enemy has different health.
  3. Build the 3D graybox route, collision/navmesh, safe spawns and gates. Measure walking times and test two clients.
  4. Place eligible resource candidate sites, fishing water regions, NPC service roles, encounters and discovery volumes; enforce density and path/slope constraints.
  5. Author quest/objective/dialogue/recipe/loot rows using those stable IDs and existing event types.
  6. Assign all references in zone/runtime/Blueprint consumers, add localization and cue IDs, validate catalogs and cook active maps.
  7. Run the full content route with empty/full inventory, novice/high-level class, party/no-party, weather, restart and transfer.
  8. Replace legal debug art incrementally; recheck capsule/foot/depth/LOS/navigation and performance after each replacement.

Density measurements

Track candidate ore/tree sites per traversable hectare, selected active nodes, enemy groups per route minute, safe-service intervals, optional landmark detour duration, and repeated-content fatigue from playtests. Proposed Rillmere fixture12ore24tree candidates and4/8active quotas are not world balance. Separate decorative foliage density from active replicated resource count.

Definition validation

Reject missing stable IDs, duplicate SiteIds, gate destinations without return paths, cyclic quests/skills, impossible tool/recipe gates, negative/zero invalid loot weights, unknown items, mutually conflicting full-outfit mappings, recipes requiring unavailable initial materials and inaccessible required services. Missing visual content may use an explicit fallback; missing economy definitions fail closed.

Expansion checklist

A new biome is ready only when its entrance/return, safe spawn, services, resources/fish, encounters, quests, map markers, localization, art provenance and measured budgets all pass. World Partition and decorative scale do not make a zone ready. Maintain a finite content backlog rather than promising endless handcrafted content.

Planned game assets are not compiled assets. Values are proposals unless explicitly evidenced. Verification and limitations.
